method: Provider Hebrew and English share exact source coordinates. Strip markup and all non-Hebrew letters to compare the source Hebrew with local paragraphs; accept only unique exact or substring matches of at least 20 letters. Source-order excerpts in each paragraph are retained in order and partial matches labeled. Additional short excerpts require a unique match within an already anchored chapter, at least eight Hebrew letters, and placement between the nearest existing source-order anchors. Further short excerpts require unique matching within source-order paragraph bounds. Two explicitly reviewed Hebrew variants use near-exact matching and are individually marked. Nine manually reviewed variants have high-overlap Hebrew matches within source-order bounds, with unmatched letters recorded. Some provider paragraphs match exact Hebrew across two adjacent local paragraphs and are explicitly labeled as continuing. Six part headings and eight short excerpts were matched using source page titles, neighboring text and contextual evidence.
limitations: Normalization does not independently establish translation quality or resolve edition differences; absent and ambiguous positions are not displayed. Provider license declaration is evidence; final release compliance is not verified.
